content.text: No non-solicitation or no-hire covenant exists anywhere in the Agreement, and § 12.3 affirmatively confirms the absence of any such restriction on us. This meets the preferred position.

input.quote: Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching covenant binding us. Searches for "solicit", "employ or engage", "induce", "hire", "recruit", "personnel", "employment", "non-compete" and review of the candidate sections (§ 12 Customer Responsibilities, § 16 Confidentiality, § 30 General) and of §§ 11, 13 turned up no restrictive covenant on Customer's hiring or solicitation of Vendor personnel. On the contrary, § 12.3 expressly confirms that nothing restricts Customer from "hiring any person who responds to general recruitment" and that Customer "has made no ... no-hire commitment". That satisfies the preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer), so the fallback narrowing elements (mutuality, scope, 12-month tail, general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs) are not engaged. Note for completeness: § 12.4 restricts Vendor from developing or marketing a competing service, which runs in our favour and is not flagged under this rule.
